newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Thirteen dead in East Timor pre-election violence.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen dead in East Timor pre-election violence.

text.p: Thirteen people were shot dead on Wednesday in a wave of pre-election violence in the Indonesian-ruled territory of East Timor, police said on Thursday.

East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam said by telephone police shot dead four rebels in a clash in the centre of the capital, Dili, on Wednesday night during an attempt to disrupt Thursday's general elections.
"From the rebels there were four dead and four captured alive. They received gunshot wounds. Four police were injured by gunfire. No police were killed," Muharam said.
"In Baucau, there were two citizens shot dead. In Los Palos, there were seven citizens shot dead and two seriously injured," he said, increasing the previous death toll by one.
He said three people were also kidnapped in the Los Palos incident.

Sources in Dili said the attack on the riot police or mobile brigade post on the outskirts of town was highly unusual and there appeared to have been some communication between the two sides before shooting took place.
Muharam said a number of polling stations in East Timor had been burned and destroyed by opponents of Indonesia's rule in the territory, invaded by Jakarta in 1975 and annexed the following year.
The United Nations still regards former colonial ruler Portugal as East Timor's administering power.
"(The rebels) wanted to threaten the people and scare them so they did not join the election. But all the people this morning have joined the election," Muharam said.
"The polling stations that were burned last night have been repaired by officials and the situation is normal this morning," he added.
Nearly 125 million people are eligible to vote in Thursday's national and local elections, in which the ruling Golkar party is assured of a comfortable victory.
